title: Emperor Fish
name: Emperor Fish (Changu)
desc: Best-loved reef fish — firm white flesh, mild taste, few bones. Fry whole, grill, or coconut sauce.

title: Tuna Fish
name: Tuna Fish (Jodari)
desc: Deep red, firm, protein-rich meat. Steaks, searing, grilling, or sushi-style.

title: Trevally Fish
name: Trevally Fish (Kolekole)
desc: Strong, meaty fish with a rich savoury taste. Frying, charcoal grilling, hearty stews.

title: Red Mullet
name: Red Mullet (Mkundaji)
desc: Delicate flesh, subtly sweet flavour. Fry whole, grill, or light coconut sauces.

title: King Fish
name: King Fish (Nguru)
desc: Pride of the Swahili coast — firm, steak-like flesh. Thick steaks, grilling, biryani.

title: Shark Steak
name: Shark Steak (Papa Mbichi)
desc: Firm, dense, boneless meat with coastal character. Frying, spiced stews.

title: Parrot Fish
name: Parrot Fish (Pono)
desc: Colourful reef fish — tender white flesh, gently sweet. Fry whole, roast, coconut sauces.

title: Red Snapper
name: Red Snapper
desc: Prized worldwide — firm white flesh, mildly sweet. Grill whole, steam, pan-fry.

title: Salmon
name: Salmon Steak (imported)
desc: Rich, buttery orange flesh with high omega-3. Sear it, roast it, or serve it raw. Imported cold-chain — the one fish on this list our boats don't catch.

title: Sardines
name: Sardines (Simusimu)
desc: Small oily fish packed with omega-3. Crispy frying, grilling, coastal stews.

title: Cobia
name: Cobia (Songoro)
desc: Cut into thick white steaks — dense like tuna but milder, with almost no small bones. Searing, grilling, frying, curries.

title: Sail Fish
name: Sail Fish (Sulisuli)
desc: Big-game ocean fish, bold distinctive flavour. Steaks, charcoal grilling, smoking.

title: Swordfish
name: Swordfish (Sulisuli Kipanga)
desc: King of the BBQ — dense steaks that hold together over hot coals. Grill, sear, skewer.

title: Rabbit Fish
name: Rabbit Fish (Tafi)
desc: Coastal classic — mild, slightly sweet, takes spices beautifully. Deep-fry whole, grill.

title: Grouper Fish
name: Grouper Fish (Tewa)
desc: White flaky flesh, mild and clean — suits almost any recipe. Fish curry, frying, coconut stews.

title: Indian Mackerel
name: Indian Mackerel (Una)
desc: Firm and flavourful, rich in natural oils. Frying, charcoal grilling, coconut curry.

title: Anchovies
name: Anchovies (Uwono)
desc: Tiny fish with intense savoury flavour. Crispy frying, spiced dishes, with ugali.

title: Red Snapper Fillets
name: Red Snapper Fillets (boneless)
desc: The fillet worth paying for — firm white flesh, mildly sweet, no bones, no scaling, no waste. Pan-sear, grill, bake, or drop straight into a coconut curry.

title: White Snapper Fillets
name: White Snapper Fillets (boneless)
desc: Clean white flesh, firm and mild — the fillet that suits every recipe and never overpowers a sauce.

title: Tilapia Fillets
name: Tilapia Fillets (boneless)
desc: Mild, tender and family-friendly — the easiest fillet to cook and the gentlest on the budget. Pan-fry, bake or stew.

title: Filleting Service
name: Red Snapper Fillets — cut from your own fish
desc: Prefer to choose your own snapper from the slab? Buy it whole and we'll fillet it for you before it goes on ice — priced by finished fillet weight.

title: Prawns Jumbo
name: Prawns Jumbo
desc: Our largest — extra-large, thick meaty flesh. Charcoal grilling, premium platters.

title: Prawns King
name: Prawns King
desc: Firm texture, rich flavour — below jumbo in size, never in quality. Grilling, pan-searing.

title: Prawns Tiger
name: Prawns Tiger
desc: Big and bold with striped shells, strong sweet taste. BBQ, curries, stews.

title: Prawns S1
name: Prawns S1
desc: The everyday workhorse of coastal cooking. Curries, stir-fries, pasta, pilau.

title: Prawns S2
name: Prawns S2
desc: Small, quick-cooking, soaks up spices beautifully. Stews, sauces, omelettes, rice.

title: Prawns Cocktail
name: Prawns Cocktail (Shrimps)
desc: Tiny, delicate, sweet — small in size, big on taste. Soups, prawn bhajia, fried rice.

title: Crab
name: Crab (Kaa)
desc: Treasured for sweet, delicate meat. Crab in coconut sauce, curries, rich soups.

title: Lobster
name: Lobster
desc: Firm texture, naturally sweet and delicate. Garlic-butter grilling, steaming, feasts.

title: Calamari · Squid
name: Calamari / Squid (Ngisi)
desc: Clean taste, tender bite when cooked fast and hot. Crispy rings, garlic butter fry, coconut curry.

title: Oysters
name: Oysters (Chaza)
desc: Shucked fresh to order. Eat them raw with lime and pilipili, grill them over charcoal, or bake with garlic butter.

title: Mussels
name: Mussels (Kome)
desc: Sweet, tender and quick — steam them open in coconut milk, garlic and chili in under ten minutes.

title: White Clams
name: White Clams
desc: Delicate and mildly sweet. Steamed with white wine or coconut, tossed through pasta, or dropped into a seafood broth.

title: Octopus
name: Octopus (Pweza)
desc: A Swahili coast delicacy — distinctive flavour, satisfying texture. Octopus in coconut sauce, grilling.

title: Dried Anchovies
name: Dried Anchovies (Katashingo)
desc: High in protein, calcium and omega-3, deep concentrated flavour. Fry crispy, boost stews and ugali.

title: Dried Sea Moss — Uncleaned
name: Dried Seamoss - Uncleaned (Mwani Mkavu)
desc: Farmed and sun-dried on the shore, natural form — rinse and soak before use. Sea moss gel, smoothies, soups.

title: Dried Sea Moss — Cleaned
name: Dried Seamoss - Cleaned (Mwani Mkavu Msafi)
desc: Washed, sorted and sun-dried golden — soak and blend straight away, no cleaning needed. Gel, smoothies, skincare.

title: Sea Moss Powder
name: Seamoss Powder (Unga wa Mwani)
desc: Ground fine — a spoonful, no soaking or blending. Smoothies, juices, soups, baking.

title: Mangrove Honey
name: Mangrove Honey (Asali ya Mikoko) — 500g jar
desc: Rare dark honey from the coastal mangrove forests of the Shimoni coast — a rich flavour ordinary honey can't match. Sealed 500g jar.

title: Dried Prawns
name: Dried Prawns (Kamba Wakavu) — 500g pack
desc: Sun-dried whole prawns with an intense, concentrated sweetness. A pinch transforms pilau, stews, coconut sauces and vegetables.

title: Dried Prawns — 1 kg
name: Dried Prawns (Kamba Wakavu) — 1 kg
desc: The full kilo for households that cook with them often, and for shops and restaurants. Same sun-dried quality, better value.

title: Barracuda
name: Barracuda (Tengesi)
desc: Long, lean hunter with firm white flesh that holds its shape. Thick steaks for the grill, chunks for curry, or fried.

title: White Mullet
name: White Mullet (Mkizi)
desc: Silver inshore fish with firm white flesh and a taste of its own — never bland. Fry it whole until the skin crisps, or score it and put it over charcoal.
